newsitem.title: TAIWAN: E.Asia Oilseeds - Taiwan to tender for soybeans.
newsitem.headline: E.Asia Oilseeds - Taiwan to tender for soybeans.

text.p: Taiwan is seen tendering for 54,000 tonnes of soybeans this week as buyers scramble to cover their positions on expectations of a rally in Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) soy futures, dealers said on Monday.
"Buyers are covering their futures positions and are likely to finish their soybean tenders this week," a trader said.
The breakfast association's Taichung division is expected to tender this week for 54,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans, they said.
Tight supplies for near-term Chicago soybean contracts and other bullish technical signals are signalling a U.S. rally.
"Near-term soybean contracts are still tight and the charts also look strong," a buyer at Taiwan's Hui Shung Agriculture and Food Corp said.
Another Taiwanese buyer said November CBOT futures could test 680 U.S. cents per bushel over the short term.
Over the past few weeks the Taiwanese have bought a total of 162,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans.
On the other hand, Japanese buyers are seen shying away from buying U.S. soybeans this week as negotiations with mills appear to be delayed, traders said.
"There're no reasons for hurrying to buy," a dealer at one of Japan's major trading houses said.
"Talks with mills for the October-December quarter have not started. They might be delayed until September as the market is bearish," the dealer said.
Another trader added that Japanese buyers may decide to wait for lower-priced new crop U.S. soybeans to become available later in the year.
